o1.biggest_strength: It correctly spots the two big hidden causes of lapse: Monsoon Dark disappearing and subscription delivery falling from 95% to 79%, and builds separate tracks for both.
o1.biggest_mistake: It does not put the 46 to 90 day at-risk buyers first, even though they are the cheapest group to save given the 34-day median reorder gap.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the 46 to 90 day group into wave 1 with reachable counts, tighten the holdout/breakeven maths, and replace the Monsoon Dark match placeholder with the actual closest current roast.

o2.biggest_strength: It rightly prioritises the at-risk 68 to 90 day buyers, calls out the 5,200 Monsoon Dark buyers, and uses holdouts and gross profit rather than coupon redemptions.
o2.biggest_mistake: The Monsoon Dark draft does not actually recommend the closest current roast, and the subscriber plan starts some ex-subscriber win-backs before the delivery problem is fully fixed.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give Monsoon Dark buyers a named replacement coffee, gate all subscriber win-back behind a delivery-date/on-time fix, and show combined email plus WhatsApp reachable counts instead of email-only reach.

reason: Output 1 is more ready to run and handles the discontinued coffee and subscription delivery problem better, with cleaner gross-profit working. Output 2 is better on the 46 to 90 day at-risk segment, but it leaves more operational gaps and its Monsoon Dark message does not deliver the promised match.
